clue.text: Bemoaning the faulty alignment

indicators.note: something faulty is out of true, so the letters of the next word are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone complains about badly lined-up parts, perhaps wheels or text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' signals the anagram of ALIGNMENT; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan something is to grieve over it aloud, which is mourning or wailing in sorrow.

clue.text: Join fellow in a dilemma

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for fellow is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a fix is an awkward predicament

explanation.surface: Join a friend who is stuck in a tricky spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts F inside A + FIX, giving A-F-FIX.
explanation.definitionFit: To affix is to attach or fasten one thing to another, which is to join them.

clue.text: Ofinterest to consumers?

parts.note: consumers here are not shoppers but eaters, and what interests an eater is food that can be swallowed

explanation.surface: Something a market researcher would flag as appealing to buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs 'Of interest' together; it reads as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything fit to be eaten is of interest to those who consume food.

clue.text: Pretty useless hanger-on?

parts.note: not a feckless parasite but a dangling ornament: pretty to look at, useless in function, and literally hanging on to a curtain or cushion

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on some idle sponger.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative bunch of threads hangs from fabric purely for looks, serving no practical purpose.

clue.text: Glen I mistook for another boy

indicators.note: the letters of Glen and I are taken wrongly, that is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to confusing one lad called Glen with a different lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistook' signals the anagram of GLENI; 'for' is a link and 'another boy' plays off Glen being a boy's name too.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel is a male given name, so it names a boy other than Glen.

clue.text: One caught fighting…

parts.note: a person taken captive during hostilities, read literally as somebody caught while at war

explanation.surface: A soldier seized during battle, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the following down clue, which continues the military picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A combatant captured by the enemy during hostilities is held as a captive of the conflict.

clue.text: … mounted an attack

parts.note: mounted usually means launched, but here it means on horseback: an assault by riders

explanation.surface: Continuing the war story: troops launched an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse soldiers rushing the enemy make an assault on horseback, literally a mounted attack.

clue.text: Indicator seen in drive

parts.note: drive suggests a private driveway or a car's indicator light, but this is a roadside device seen while driving

explanation.surface: A car's blinker noticed on the way up a driveway.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured lights at junctions tell motorists when to stop and go while they are driving.

clue.text: Errand-boy creates confusion before turning green

indicators.note: before places the word for confusion ahead of the remaining letters

parts.note: a mess is a state of disorder

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of green are twisted into another order

explanation.surface: A delivery lad causes chaos before going green with sickness, or with envy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes ENGER, an anagram of GREEN; 'creates' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand-boy carries messages and parcels for others, which is a courier's job.

clue.text: I clean out in order to inject

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them, so the three words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse wipes the skin clean before giving a jab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' signals the anagram of ICLEANOUT; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To inoculate is to introduce a vaccine into the body, typically by injection.

clue.text: Some slackness exposed by the cricket team

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cricket side has its lazy play shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county with a first-class cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex County Cricket Club is one of the first-class county sides in English cricket.

clue.text: Get to know name of king first

indicators.note: first says the king goes ahead of the abbreviation for name

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king

explanation.surface: Find out a monarch's name before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something is to acquire knowledge of it.

clue.text: Refashioned Levi's can still be worn

definitions.text: Refashioned Levi's can still be worn

indicators.note: refashioned means remade in a new form, so the brand name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: Levi's is the jeans brand, its S part of the name

explanation.surface: Remodelled jeans are still wearable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refashioned' signals the anagram of LEVIS; the whole clue also describes the answer, items that are worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Veils are face coverings of fine fabric, garments worn on the head.

clue.text: Lord taken in by doctor, that's plain

indicators.note: taken in by means the abbreviation for Lord goes inside the word for doctor

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A peer is fooled by a physician, and that's plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' has the sense 'deceived by' on the surface; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The veldt is the open grassland of southern Africa, a flat treeless expanse.

clue.text: Strong fibre cracked tiles

indicators.note: cracked means broken up, so the letters of tiles are scrambled

explanation.surface: Tough fibres have cracked the roof tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' signals the anagram of TILES. Istle is a plant fibre used for cord and brushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a tough fibre from Mexican agave and yucca plants, used for cordage.

clue.text: Kim's maybe about right to produce an affected smile

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for right
maybe hints that the letters given could be arranged some other way

parts.note: the name with its S counted as letters

explanation.surface: Perhaps Kim, being right, wears a self-satisfied grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' gives SMIK, an anagram of KIMS, and 'about' puts it around R: SMI-R-K. 'to produce' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A smirk is a smug, insincere grin, a smile that is put on.

clue.text: Record run

definitions.meaning: a disc released with one main song
one run scored between the wickets in cricket

explanation.surface: A two-word note that something set a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A single is a short record with one main track; in cricket a single is one run scored.

clue.text: System used by yours truly does not completely deceive

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

indicators.note: not completely means the last letter of the word for deceive is dropped

parts.note: to trick someone is to deceive them

explanation.surface: Someone insists their method is not a total con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' is a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The decimal measuring scheme of metres and kilograms is one particular system of units.

clue.text: The French hit out using a heavy stick

parts.note: la is a French word for the

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of hit are put out of order

explanation.surface: French police strike out with a cudgel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes THI, an anagram of HIT; 'using' is a link. A lathi is a bamboo staff used by police in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a long iron-bound bamboo staff, a heavy club used by Indian police.

clue.text: Sea-nymph from Tyneside area has bumpy ride

parts.note: Tyneside is in north-east England, abbreviated NE

indicators.note: a bumpy ride jolts things about, so the letters of ride are shaken up

explanation.surface: A water spirit from Newcastle has a rough journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumpy' makes EREID, an anagram of RIDE; 'from' and 'has' are links. Tyneside is the area around Newcastle upon Tyne.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Nereids were the fifty sea-nymph daughters of Nereus.

clue.text: Rogue artist by burn finishes early

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: finishes early means the word stops short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to scald is to burn with hot liquid

explanation.surface: A rogue painter beside a stream stops work early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burn' looks like a Scottish stream beside the artist; it means scald. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous or dishonest person, a scamp.

clue.text: Little woman in the wood has a twitch

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for woman inside the word for wood

parts.note: teak is a hardwood
little signals the short form: W abbreviates woman

explanation.surface: A small lady in a forest suffers a nervous tic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a sharp sudden pull or jerk, a small twitching movement.

clue.text: Suggestion given with a shout of pain that there is an opening in the wall

parts.note: wind means a hint, as in getting wind of something
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: Someone yelps while hinting there is a hole in the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given with' and 'that there is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A window is a glazed gap in a wall that lets in light.

clue.text: Business concern

definitions.meaning: a matter or piece of business

explanation.surface: Two words a company report might use about the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or business, and also a matter of concern, as in 'that's my affair'.

clue.text: Of little folk who are not completely self-indulgent

indicators.note: not completely says only part of the hyphenated word is used, a run from inside it

explanation.surface: Some small people are only partly greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means relating to elves, the small folk of fairy tales.

clue.text: She's exact about one point

indicators.note: about means the word for exact goes around the point of the compass

parts.note: nice can mean precise, as in a nice distinction
E, east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: A woman is precise about a single detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She's' is She plus a link 's for 'is'; NICE in its old sense 'precise' is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a female relative, so she can stand for one.

clue.text: Redhead in hot weather is a card

indicators.note: in places the head letter of red inside the word for hot weather

parts.note: a heat or heatwave is a spell of hot weather
the head of the word red is its first letter

explanation.surface: A ginger-haired person in a heatwave is a real character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' is read as red's head, its first letter R; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart is a playing card of the red suit marked with heart symbols.

clue.text: Henry goes over the south-eastern port

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means sitting above, so Henry comes first

parts.note: Hy is a short form of Henry

explanation.surface: King Henry travels across to a Kent harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Hythe is one of the Cinque Ports on the Kent coast in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hythe is a Cinque Port town on the coast of Kent in south-east England.

clue.text: Exploit an opportunity to gain a point on court

definitions.meaning: make the most of a chance
in tennis, win the point after deuce

explanation.surface: Advice to a tennis player to seize a chance to win a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To take advantage is to exploit a chance; in tennis, taking advantage means winning the point after deuce.

clue.text: Typist, she is essential to her boss

definitions.text: Typist, she is essential to her boss

parts.words: Typist, she is essential to her boss
parts.note: a typist works the keys of a keyboard, and a vital member of staff is the most important one

explanation.surface: A tribute to an indispensable secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: A typist presses keys all day, and an essential staff member is a pivotal employee.
